t.E415.agn: In 2017 EFSA saw no need for a numerical acceptable daily intake (ADI) and found no safety concern for the general population; abdominal discomfort at high doses was reported, which was not considered an adverse effect.
t.E415.body: Xanthan gum is not absorbed unchanged; it is partly fermented by bacteria in the large intestine.
t.E415.eff.0.t: Abdominal discomfort has been reported; EFSA did not consider this an adverse effect
t.E415.prod: Produced by fermentation with the bacterium Xanthomonas campestris.
t.E415.regx.0: Re-evaluated; no numerical ADI needed, no safety concern for the general population.
t.E415.regx.1: Purity criteria updated (heavy metal limits lowered); from 18.08.2026.
t.E415.summary: A thickener produced by fermenting sugar with bacteria. Very common in sauces, salad dressings and gluten-free products.
t.E415.what: Thickens even in small amounts and stabilises mixtures.
